title: The column that arrived on Tuesday
outcome: A supplier added a field, Auto Loader stopped exactly as designed, and nothing restarted it, so bronze sat still for a night.

content.bookmark: In its default mode, Auto Loader stops on a new column after recording it, and picks it up on restart. Run it as a job that restarts, or the stop becomes an outage.

check.prompt: Auto Loader infers the schema (no schema given). A file arrives with a new column. What happens by default?
options: The new column is dropped and the stream carries on
The stream fails with an unknown-field error after recording the column, and uses it on restart
The stream keeps running, writes the new column as null, and waits for someone to approve the schema change by hand
check.why: The default mode without a given schema is addNewColumns: the stream records the new column, fails with UnknownFieldException, and resumes with the new schema when it restarts.

check.prompt: Which schema evolution mode never fails the stream and never adds columns?
check.why: In rescue mode the schema never evolves and the stream never fails: values for new columns go to the rescued data column.

check.prompt: JSON files, no schema hints, cloudFiles.inferColumnTypes not set. What type does inference give each column?
options: The narrowest type that fits the sampled values
The type of the matching column in the target table
check.why: For JSON, CSV and XML, every column is inferred as string unless cloudFiles.inferColumnTypes is true.

check.prompt: Where does Auto Loader keep the schema it inferred?
options: In the target table's properties, updated each time a micro-batch commits
In the job's parameters, which the stream rewrites when the schema changes
check.why: The inferred schema and its changes are stored in a _schemas directory at the schema location, which can be the checkpoint path.

caseStudy.setting: A home-goods retailer (fictional) receives order files as JSON from its suppliers into a Unity Catalog volume. An Auto Loader stream in a notebook loads them into a bronze table. The notebook runs as a single-task job every night, with no retry policy and nothing set to restart it.

events.what: One supplier starts sending a new field, discount_code. The nightly run fails with UnknownFieldException a few minutes in.
The sales dashboard shows no orders since Tuesday. An engineer reruns the job by hand; it succeeds, and the new column appears in bronze.
In the review, someone proposes switching to rescue mode "so it never fails again". Someone else asks why a rerun fixed it without any code change.

pipeline: Auto Loader (cloudFiles) · schema inferred, schemaLocation set, default evolution mode
Lakeflow job · one notebook task, nightly schedule, no retries
tasks: Why did the stream fail, and why did a rerun fix it?
Should the team switch to rescue mode?

debrief.title: Why it stopped, and why the rerun worked
text: Nothing broke. With no schema given, Auto Loader's default mode is addNewColumns: it records the new column at the schema location, then fails the stream with UnknownFieldException.
On restart it resumes with the new schema. The manual rerun was simply that restart, which is why no code change was needed.

debrief.title: Why it stayed down all night
text: The design assumes something restarts the stream. Databricks recommends running Auto Loader as a Lakeflow job that restarts automatically for exactly this reason.
Here the job had no retry policy, so the expected stop became a ten-hour gap. A retry policy set explicitly on the task would have restarted it after the retry interval, not the next morning.

debrief.title: Choosing the mode
text: rescue never fails, but new fields land in the _rescued_data column, not in a column of their own. That suits a bronze table that must never stop, if someone checks the rescued column.
addNewColumns keeps the schema growing with the source, with a restart each time. failOnNewColumns suits a strict contract: the stream stops until the schema or the file is fixed.
Databricks' medallion guidance adds a third option for bronze: keep most fields as strings or VARIANT, so schema surprises don't drop data.

takeaway: addNewColumns stops on a new column by design; a restart picks it up.
Run Auto Loader as a job that restarts automatically.
Pick the evolution mode as a decision about who notices new fields.
content.honesty: If you haven't run Auto Loader in production, say so, and explain the evolution modes and why the stream needs to restart. If you have seen a schema change stop a pipeline, start with that.

tasks: What would you ask the team about the source?
What should the definition of done for a new source include?

debrief.title: Questions
text: "Do suppliers tell us before they change their files, and who hears about it?"
"If a new field arrives, do we want it in the data straight away, or reviewed first?"

debrief.title: Definition of done
text: The ingestion job restarts on its own after a failure.
The chosen schema evolution mode, and who is told when the schema changes, are written down.

sayIt.question: A data feed you depend on changes its format without warning. How do you make the product resilient to that?
points: Assume sources will change and design for it.
Decide whether new fields flow through automatically or wait for review.
Make sure the pipeline recovers on its own from an expected stop.
Have someone notified when the shape of the data changes.
Agree change notice with the source's owners where possible.

tasks: What do you tell the sales team on Wednesday morning?
What should change so this costs minutes, not a night?

debrief.title: Wednesday morning
text: Orders since Tuesday night are missing from the dashboard; the load has been rerun and the numbers are now complete. Nothing was lost.

debrief.title: Minutes, not a night
text: An automatic restart on the job, and a failure notification to someone who can act. The review should be about the missing restart, not the supplier.

sayIt.question: A nightly data load failed and nobody noticed until morning. How do you handle it?
points: Restore the data first and tell users what was affected.
Find why it failed and why nobody knew.
Add automatic recovery for failures that are expected.
Route failure alerts to someone who can act.
Review blamelessly and track the fixes.

tasks: What actions come out of the review?
How do you settle the rescue-mode debate?

debrief.title: Actions
text: Add a retry policy to the ingestion task and a failure notification, with an owner and a date.
Check every other Auto Loader job for the same gap.

debrief.title: The debate
text: Frame it as a choice of who notices new fields: the stream restarts with them (addNewColumns), or they wait in _rescued_data for review (rescue). Let the data owner choose.

sayIt.question: How would you make sure a fix from an incident review is applied everywhere, not just on the job that failed?
points: Turn the finding into a standard, such as every ingestion job restarts automatically.
Find every job the standard applies to.
Give each fix an owner and a date.
Check it in deployment or review, not by memory.
Close the action only when it is verified.

tasks: What would you change in the job and the stream?
How would you test the change?

debrief.title: Changes
text: Set a retry policy on the task (count and interval) so the stream restarts after UnknownFieldException.
Keep addNewColumns if new fields should flow through; add schema hints for fields whose types matter, or set cloudFiles.inferColumnTypes.

debrief.title: Testing
text: Drop a file with an extra field into a test volume and confirm the job fails once, restarts, and the column appears.
Check that _rescued_data stays empty for well-formed files.

sayIt.question: Explain how Auto Loader handles schema inference and evolution.
points: The schema is inferred from a sample and stored under cloudFiles.schemaLocation.
JSON, CSV and XML columns are strings unless inferColumnTypes is true; schema hints override types.
addNewColumns (the default without a schema) records the column, fails, and resumes on restart.
rescue never fails and puts unexpected values in _rescued_data; failOnNewColumns stops until fixed.
Run it as a job that restarts automatically.
